newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open lower with Dow.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open lower with Dow.

text.p: Australian stocks opened broadly lower on Monday, taking their cue from a weaker Wall Street and a discounted futures market.

"We're just following the Dow and the All Ords seems to be dragged down by the SPI (share price index futures) contract -- that's dictating the terms," said Burdett, Buckridge and Young dealer Stephen Smith.
The March share price index futures contract was up two points at 2,429.0 at 10.45 a.m. (2345), at a discount to the All Ordinaries Index, which was down 15.4 points at 2,434.5.
The Dow closed 47.33 points lower at 6,877.44 on Friday on increasing nervousness in the wake of Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's cautionary comments last week.
U.S. analysts expect the market nervousness to continue until Greenspan's next Humphrey Hawkins address on Wednesday.
Locally, stocks were generally half a percent to a percent lower across the board, with the banks leading the market down.
The Commonwealth Bank of Australia, which has flown high in recent months, was down 20 cents or 1.5 percent at A$12.62, while National Australia Bank Ltd was down 13 cents at A$16.09.
Miner RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd led the resources sector down, losing 31.2 cents to be A$18.98 after falling in London on Friday on negative comments in the British press.

Bougainville Copper Ltd, however, surged five cents or almost nine percent to 61 cents after the Papua New Guinea government said on Sunday it wanted to buy CRA's controlling stake in Bougainville's Panguna copper mine.
Traders, however, remained wary of over-enthusiasm about the offer, saying they would prefer to wait for more concrete signs before pushing Bougainville higher.
Other stocks to buck the downward trend in early trade were Cultus Petroleum NL, which rose 13 cents to A$2.25, racing further ahead after its announcement of a small oil find in the Otway Basin.
Brambles Industries Ltd also rose 10 cents to A$21.80 after its strong first half result released on Friday.

HIH Winterthur Ltd rose two cents to A$3.11 after it announced a year net profit of A$61.5 million (US$48 million), which was within market expectations. However, its commentary was bullish, saying considerable premium growth was assured.
